theory.title: Hablar de cambios y de acostumbrarse
theory.explanation: Used to + infinitivo describe hábitos o situaciones del pasado que ya no son iguales: I used to live with my parents. Be used to + sustantivo o verbo en -ing significa estar acostumbrado a algo: I'm used to living alone. Get used to + sustantivo o verbo en -ing expresa el proceso de acostumbrarse: It took me a month to get used to my new routine. Después de una preposición como to en be/get used to, utiliza un sustantivo o gerundio, no el infinitivo. Para explicar consecuencias, utiliza as a result, so y because.
theory.tip: Compara el significado: I used to get up late (antes solía levantarme tarde); I'm used to getting up early (ahora estoy acostumbrado/a); I'm getting used to getting up early (me estoy acostumbrando).

patterns.label: Used to + infinitivo: hábitos pasados
patterns.pattern: Used to + verbo base: hábito o estado pasado que ha cambiado.
examples:
I used to be shy.
→ Antes era tímido/a.

patterns.label: Be used to + nombre/-ing: estar acostumbrado
patterns.pattern: Am/is/are/was/were used to + sustantivo o gerundio.
examples:
I'm used to the noise.
→ Ella solía ir al trabajo en autobús.

patterns.label: Get used to + nombre/-ing: acostumbrarse
patterns.pattern: Get/become used to + sustantivo o gerundio: proceso de adaptación.
examples:
I'm getting used to my new school.
→ Estoy acostumbrado/a al ruido.

patterns.label: Negativas y preguntas con used to
patterns.pattern: Didn't use to + verbo base; Did + sujeto + use to + verbo base?
examples:
I didn't use to enjoy exercise.
→ Él está acostumbrado a trabajar bajo presión.

patterns.label: Diferencia entre used to y be used to
patterns.pattern: Used to habla del pasado; be used to habla de familiaridad actual o pasada.
examples:
I used to work nights.
→ Me estoy acostumbrando a mi nueva escuela.

patterns.label: Get used to en distintos tiempos
patterns.pattern: Cambia get según el tiempo verbal; conserva used to + sustantivo/-ing.
examples:
You'll get used to it.
→ Costó tiempo acostumbrarse a vivir en el extranjero.

patterns.label: Because: expresar una razón
patterns.pattern: Because + oración para explicar la causa.
examples:
I changed jobs because I wanted a new challenge.
→ Antes no disfrutaba haciendo ejercicio.

patterns.label: So/as a result: expresar consecuencias
patterns.pattern: So conecta causa y resultado; as a result introduce una consecuencia.
examples:
The journey was long, so I moved closer.
→ ¿Vivías aquí antes?

patterns.label: Take up y give up: empezar y dejar
patterns.pattern: Take up + actividad para empezar; give up + actividad/sustantivo o -ing para dejar.
examples:
I took up swimming.
→ Antes trabajaba de noche.

patterns.label: Make a decision/progress: tomar decisiones y progresar
patterns.pattern: Utiliza make con decision y progress.
examples:
I made an important decision.
→ Ahora estoy acostumbrado/a a trabajar de noche.

content.passage: When Elena finished university, she had to decide what to do next. She used to live in a small town and had never considered moving far away. Then she was offered a job in Manchester. It was a difficult choice because she was close to her family, but she wanted to become more independent. During the first weeks, she found the city noisy and missed her old routine. She wasn't used to travelling on crowded trains or cooking every evening. However, she slowly got used to her new life. She joined a running club and made friends at work. As a result, she became more confident and discovered that she enjoyed new challenges. Looking back, she says that accepting the job was a turning point. She still visits her family regularly, but she no longer depends on them for everyday decisions.

items.prompt: Describe a decision that changed your daily routine.
items.modelAnswer: A decision that changed my routine was starting an evening course. I used to spend my evenings watching television, but now I study twice a week. It was difficult at first, but I'm used to the new schedule.

items.prompt: Talk about something you used to do but don't do now.
items.modelAnswer: I used to play video games every evening. I enjoyed it, but I wanted to be more active, so I took up cycling.

items.prompt: Describe a new situation you had to get used to.
items.modelAnswer: When I started my first job, I had to get used to travelling early and working with new people. It took a few weeks, but now I feel comfortable.

items.prompt: Explain how you became more independent.
items.modelAnswer: I became more independent when I moved away to study. I had to manage my money and cook for myself. As a result, I learned to organise my time.

items.prompt: Talk about a challenge that helped you make progress.
items.modelAnswer: Learning to drive was a challenge for me. I made mistakes, but my instructor encouraged me. Eventually, I passed the test.

items.prompt: Describe a habit you would like to change.
items.modelAnswer: I'd like to stop checking my phone before bed. I know it affects my sleep, so I'm trying to read instead.

items.prompt: Talk about a time you stepped out of your comfort zone.
items.modelAnswer: I joined a drama group even though I was shy. At first I felt uncomfortable, but the other members supported me.

items.prompt: Explain the difference between used to and be used to with your own examples.
items.modelAnswer: I used to get up late when I was at school. Now I'm used to getting up early because I start work at eight.

items.prompt: Describe an opportunity you decided to accept or reject.
items.modelAnswer: I accepted an opportunity to volunteer abroad. I was worried about the language, but it helped me become more confident.

items.prompt: Talk for two minutes about a turning point in your life and its consequences.
items.modelAnswer: One turning point was deciding to study English seriously. I used to avoid speaking, but I practised regularly. As a result, I'm more confident and can communicate with more people.

content.audioTranscript: Sam: Have you always lived in this city? Priya: No. I used to live in a village, but I moved here for university. Sam: Was it difficult to adapt? Priya: Yes, at first. I wasn't used to the traffic or the busy streets. Sam: How did you get used to it? Priya: I started cycling to class and joined a photography group. Sam: Did you find it easy to make friends? Priya: Not immediately. I was quite shy, but the group encouraged me to join their weekend trips. Sam: And what happened after that? Priya: I became more confident. As a result, I started volunteering at a local centre. Sam: Do you miss your old home? Priya: Sometimes, but I enjoy my life here now.
